title: Biological age acceleration and urinary incontinence: A combined analysis from two national cohorts in the United States and China
content:
by Ping Kong, Zhangxiang Chen, Zhiqi Liu, Haibing Wang, Zhiqiang Zhang

Background

To explore the relationship between the GOLD biological age difference (GOLD BioAgeDiff)—a quantitative measure of aging—and urinary incontinence using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).

Materials and methods

In NHANES, weighted multinomial logistic regression assessed UI subtypes, ordinal logistic regression assessed severity; additional analyses included propensity score matching (PSM), restricted cubic splines (RCSs), subgroup analyses, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). In CHARLS, Cox models and Kaplan-Meier curves evaluated incident UI.

Results

GOLD BioAgeDiff was associated with urge (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04) and mixed UI (OR 1.02, 95% CI: 1.00–1.03), but not stress UI. Each 1-unit increase raised severe UI odds by 3% (OR 1.03); the highest quartile had 52% higher risk (OR 1.52). A nonlinear relationship was observed (P < 0.001); no interaction remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons in exploratory subgroup analyses. XGBoost ranked GOLD BioAgeDiff as a key predictor. In CHARLS, Light BioAgeDiff predicted incident UI (HR 1.01, 1.00–1.02).

Conclusions

GOLD BioAgeDiff is significantly associated with UI severity, subtype, and incidence—especially for urge and mixed UI. As a quantifiable marker of biological aging, it may provide complementary information for risk stratification in population-based settings.
author: Ping Kong
